  • Pascua Yaqui↗Specific government / administrative location
    Connection & source
    Specific government / administrative location

    The Tribe’s own departmental page locates the Pascua Yaqui administration in Tucson, Arizona. This is a specific government-location route, not the full historical geography of Yaqui/Yoeme peoples on both sides of the international border. Inspection: Actual departmental remit and tribal address, especially lines 172–175. No claim that an undated personnel listing remains current.

    Undated tribal departmental page; inspected October 21, 2026. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Yavapai↗Constituent people within present government

    Constituent people within present government

    The Nation explicitly locates itself in Arizona's Verde Valley and identifies Yavapai and Apache as two distinct constituent peoples. This links one Yavapai community; it does not subsume all Yavapai governments.

    Present tribal government location

  • Yuma↗Quechan / Yuma language name access point
    Connection & source
    Quechan / Yuma language name access point

    The Tribe locates its community on the Colorado River near Yuma, Arizona. This route uses Yuma in the Quechan-name scope documented by Miller's introductory language discussion. Inspection: Opening Colorado River / Arizona location paragraph. Limits: Quechan access point only; bordering Baja California does not establish a Mexico residence.

    Community location described by the Tribe, page updated 2025-05-09. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

These are starting lists, not a complete census. Modern borders help you navigate; they are not Indigenous homeland boundaries. A connection may be historical or present-day and does not imply presence throughout a region. Directory names can overlap; the profiles explain their relationships.
